what: capture_corpus.py rejected --full-cache-lengths; argparse had no such option
cause: a str.replace() patch matched a literal default list against a line reading default=LENGTHS, so it replaced nothing and returned the string unchanged. The two lines consuming the option landed; the add_argument did not. The edit was written without an assertion while a sibling edit in the same patch had one, and only the unasserted edit failed
resolution: option added with assertions on both the match and its absence; verified through --help rather than by grepping for the name, which is what made it look present

what: negative test 'truncated_payload' reported MISSED; B0 failed
cause: the test declared half the compressed size and left the bytes in place. cuSZp's decompress never reads the cmpSize argument, so it consumed the whole payload and returned a correct reconstruction. The validator was right and the test was wrong
measurements_invalidated: none -- B0 gates and it stopped
resolution: the test now removes the bytes, which is what a truncated transfer is. The cmpSize behaviour is recorded as an observation: declaring 64 bytes in place of 628,536 returns a bit-identical decode, and only removing bytes breaks it, at 245x eps
became_finding: b0_findings.md -- gives the previously-inferred zeroed-buffer contract a mechanism

what: B1 stopped at held-out article 16 of 32: E32=1.46512 against eps=1.46512, exceeding eps + 1e-6
cause: the pre-declared absolute tolerance has the wrong shape. cuSZp exceeds its bound by up to 1.0000015x eps -- a few float32 ulps of eps, from a quantiser working off a float32 1/eps. The excess is relative, so it clears an absolute 1e-6 at small eps and fails at large. B0 saw 0 of 448 failures with eps <= 2.2
detected_by: the acceptance check, working as written
measurements_invalidated: the 15 articles scored before the abort were discarded; B1 was re-run whole
resolution: TAU was NOT widened. The fp32 margin became a recorded measurement on every tensor and the abort was reserved for damage (>1.001x eps). The consequence is stated: this round does not certify E32 <= eps + 1e-6
became_finding: correction 23; b0_findings.md proposes the relative form for next round

what: CUDA illegal memory access after 120 of 360 pairs, aborting the process
cause: the pre/post verification assumed the compressed arm had run last. Arms share the buffers and the file and the pair order is shuffled on purpose, so when a block ended on raw, check_written read a 117 MB raw bf16 file as a 39 MB compressed stream and handed the decoder block offsets made of garbage. check_moved had the same flaw and failed silently, comparing raw output against the compressed criterion
detected_by: the CUDA runtime; located with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1, since the reported stack was a tensor destructor where the deferred fault surfaced
measurements_invalidated: all 120 pairs from the first attempt were discarded; B2 was re-run whole
resolution: verification now runs an arm and then checks that arm, for both arms, at the start and end of every block -- strictly more coverage, and it cannot verify something it did not produce. Also corrected the bf16 rounding allowance, which scaled by the error instead of the data magnitude

what: a `global DEPTH` was placed after a use of DEPTH in the same function; ast.parse accepted it
cause: syntax checking in this round used ast.parse, which does not run the symbol-table pass that rejects a late global declaration. compile() does
detected_by: compile() check added after the fact
resolution: fixed, and every script in scripts/ and boundrelay/ now compile-checks clean
